newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian capital quiet after fighting.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian capital quiet after fighting.

text.p: Phnom Penh was quiet but tense as dawn broke on Monday but many residents feared a new round of fighting as forces loyal to the country's rival prime ministers faced off to the west of the city.
An explosion boomed across the Cambodian capital from the west just as a 6 a.m. (2300 GMT) curfew ended after a night punctuated by intermittent bursts of small-arms fire.
At least 12 people were killed and more than 50 wounded in a weekend of fighting on the streets of the capital.
On Monday troops loyal to powerful second prime minister Hun Sen manned checkpoints on city streets and also blocked the road to the airport.

Forces loyal to first prime minister prince Norodom Ranariddh still controlled areas to the west of Phnom Penh, including Tang Krasang military base just to the north of the city's airport, 10 km (six miles) west of Phnom Penh.
A resident in the west of the city said he could hear automatic weapons fire, and hundreds of people were streaming out of a neighbourhood between the city centre and the airport.
Hun Sen's forces had cut all access to the airport, witnesses said.
"Absolutely everything is blocked off, there is no way to get to the west of the city," a foreign news photographer said.
All flights in and out of Phnom Penh were cancelled, leaving hundreds of foreigners stranded in the city since the weekend. Many of the stranded were in temporary accommodations.
Hun Sen's forces captured the headquarters of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and his city centre residence in heavy fighting on Sunday.
Thousands of Phnom Penh residents fled the city at the weekend by bus, truck and boat.
It was unclear whether fighting was going on in other parts of Cambodia. There had been reports on Saturday of clashes in the south, but none could be independently confirmed.
Hun Sen said in a radio broadcast late on Sunday that Ranariddh was a traitor and no longer held the post of first prime minister.
He called on the prince's party to chose a new person to fill the job. Ranariddh said in a statement from Paris at the weekend that Hun Sen had launched a coup against him.
The two leaders have shared power in a coalition government set up after a 1993 election organised by the United Nations.
